newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European markets follow Dow off highs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European markets follow Dow off highs.

text.p: Several European stock markets hit all-time highs on Wednesday as Wall Street extended its record run initially, but all the markets eased back after a Federal Reserve vice-chairman's comments.

Vice-chairman Alice Rivlin said "there seems to be little risk of the (U.S.) economy slowing down too much in the near-term and sliding into recession. The risks seem higher on the other side, that many of the factors holding down inflationary pressures will prove temporary."

Germany, France, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Austria notched record highs while other bourses held sharply higher levels as the Dow Jones Industrial Average added about 80 points to Tuesday's 155-point gain before edging off on some profit-taking after Rivlin's comments.
The Dow pared gains and was up only 24.38 points at 8,086.03 in late European trading.
The dollar also gave back some gains after Rivlin said the currency may not get much stronger.

Earlier, the dollar jumped to a six-year high against the mark and a one-year high against the French franc, which added lustre to German and French export shares as the weaker currencies make their goods cheaper abroad.
The dollar was also supported by general mark weakness from continuing uncertainty over European economic and monetary union.

But gold, traditionally used as an inflation hedge, sagged with Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's forecast on Tuesday for tame inflation this year. Greenspan said recent sharp declines in gold prices were more reflective of low inflation expectations than central bank sales.

Germany's DAX index surged 4.15 percent to post its biggest daily gain this year and ended bourse trading up 175.67 points at 4,406.09. But that was off its intraday high of 4,418.64, scored before bourse trade was temporarily suspended just after midday due to a systems problem.
Some analysts in Frankfurt were predicting the DAX above 5,000 within the next two weeks.
Paris added about three percent, to score a record high of 3,026.99 after Wall Street opened.
Italian stocks got an added lift from tame July inflation data. Preliminary July consumer price data showed inflation flat from June and at a 1.6-percent pace, year-over-year.
Italy's blue-chip Mib30 index hit a record 23,375 and the all-share Mibtel notched a record 15,311.
Belgium jumped nearly 2.5 percent to a record high 2,606.88 on Wall Street's tails.
Austria's ATX index climbed 3.15 percent to an all-time high of 1,452.78.

French, German, Italian and British government debt prices also rallied to new highs, lowering interest rates and lending even more support to stocks. U.S. 30-year bond yields also slid at New York's open to 6.41 percent, the lowest level since December 5.
"Greenspan is painting a picture of moderate growth and inflation under control, and all bond markets like that," a dealer on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange said.

"Interest rates are falling, stock markets are rising...and everything is fine," said a broker in Helsinki, where the FOX index rose about 1.8 percent in early trade but remained short of its all-time high of 1,226.84 set on July 17.

Banking shares in Germany's DAX index and France's CAC-40 index led gains with help from merger speculation and solid earnings reports. Monday's news that Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypobank would merge had already fired up investors, believing that a long-awaited consolidation of the fragmented banking sector might be under way.

Germany's largest bank, Deutsche Bank AG helped sentiment by reporting a 27.5 percent rise in net income. The result, above forecasts, sent its shares surging to an all-time high of 132 before easing back to about 124.70, or up 8.05 marks, in mid-afternoon.
Banque Nationale de Paris and Crdit Commercial de France in France also climbed. Credit Commercial gained more than 10 percent to notch a year high of 300.0.
London's FTSE-100 index also rose, but gains were more restrained, easing as the Dow slipped off its record high.
Greenspan will finish his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony later on Wednesday.
CURRENCIES AT 1520 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8265 marks and 115.85 yen versus 1.8177 and 115.54 in late trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1520 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 26.1 points at 4,872.80.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended bourse trade up 175.67 points at 4,406.09.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 82.40 points at 3,003.53.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in London at 1500 GMT at $324.90, down from $327.95 at Tuesday's close. Silver was firm at $4.33 .
